changes.after: You can no longer move advisors into an occupied territory and turn them into fighters on arrival. A moving group also cannot flip merely to join your opposite-face group at its destination.

changes.before: A city empties after your chance to flip
changes.after: A stronghold empties during movement

changes.before: Your advisors become the only force in a stronghold after Shipping and Movement has begun. They remain advisors. They do not suddenly control it, collect spice, gain ornithopters or block entry.
changes.after: If your advisors are left alone after Shipping and Movement begins, they stay advisors. They cannot control the stronghold, collect spice, gain ornithopters or block entry.

changes.before: You may ship normally into your fighters or a territory without your own tokens. Do not use the old allowance to ship into your advisors as a general way around the new face restrictions.
changes.after: Normal paid shipment uses fighters. You may ship into your fighters or a territory without your own tokens. The old general permission to ship into your advisors no longer applies.

changes.before: A moving fighter group can become advisors
changes.after: Fighters may become advisors when moving

changes.before: Entering another faction's territory where you had no forces can permit that change. If the other faction is your ally, the new text requires it. This does not grant a reciprocal advisor-to-fighter change mid-phase.
changes.after: When moving into another faction's territory where you had no forces, fighters may be allowed to become advisors. If that faction is your ally, they must. This permission does not allow advisors to become fighters during the phase.

changes.before: The new wording includes another faction deploying in, not just shipping or moving. The accompanying-advisor rule also retains its specific exception allowing existing fighters to become advisors before the free advisor is placed.
changes.after: Intrusion now includes another faction deploying forces, as well as shipping or moving. When placing an accompanying advisor, you may still turn existing fighters into advisors before placing it, as specified by that ability.

changes.before: The specific advisor rules support coexistence with your ally; the general alliance constraint does not repeat that exemption. This guide uses the specific faction text and keeps the cross-reference tension flagged.
changes.after: The advisor rules allow coexistence with an ally, but the general alliance paragraph does not repeat the exemption. The specific Bene Gesserit rule allows it; the cross-reference remains unclear.

changes.before: Fremen: storm knowledge and worm events
changes.after: Fremen: storms and sandworms

changes.before: Start with four rather than three. The normal starting distribution, two-territory movement and three free revivals remain familiar.
changes.after: Fremen starts with four spice instead of three. Its initial force placement, two-territory movement and three free revivals are unchanged.

changes.before: Inspect the next top Storm card
changes.after: Storm Insight

changes.before: Storm Insight now reads the shared deck at the end of Storm. You no longer select, return and reshuffle a private card each round.
changes.after: At the end of Storm, inspect the top card of the shared Storm deck. Fremen no longer selects, returns and reshuffles a private card each round.

changes.before: The older FAQ prohibited normal movement or worm rides into or out of storm. The new sheet permits shipment, a one-territory move, and a worm ride into storm at the stated half loss. Do not turn this into unrestricted storm transit or a general permission to leave storm.
changes.after: The older FAQ prohibited normal movement and worm rides into or out of storm. The new sheet allows shipment, a one-territory move or a worm ride into storm, with the stated half loss. It does not allow unrestricted travel through storm or general movement out of it.

changes.before: Half means tokens
changes.after: Count tokens for storm losses

changes.before: Three entering forces, including any Fedaykin, lose half rounded up: two tokens. A Fedaykin is one token for storm loss, even though its battle strength is two. You may choose to lose more or all of the group.
changes.after: A group of three entering forces loses two tokens, half rounded up. A Fedaykin counts as one token for this loss, despite its battle strength of two. You may choose to lose more, including the whole group.

changes.before: One permission is not an extra movement chain
changes.after: Limits on storm movement

changes.before: The new example does not permit shipping into storm and then moving into another storm territory. A worm ride jumps to a destination sector rather than tracing an ordinary movement path.
changes.after: The new example does not allow shipment into storm followed by movement to another storm territory. A worm ride goes directly to its destination sector rather than following a normal movement path.

changes.before: Cancellation no longer removes these powers
changes.after: Karama targets Battle Edge

changes.before: The single vulnerable advantage is Battle Edge. Old Karama options against Storm Insight, storm protection, movement and worm riding are not imported into the new cancellation list.
changes.after: Karama can no longer cancel Storm Insight, storm protection, movement or worm riding. Battle Edge is the sole vulnerable advantage.

changes.before: Additional worms use one phase-wide sequence
changes.after: Call Sandworms uses one sequence per phase

changes.before: The new Call Sandworms applies to subsequent Shai-Hulud after the first drawn in the phase, with placed worms resolved at the end of Nexus. Our old GF9 book explicitly used per-pile handling. The original printed faction sentence was less explicit about that reset, so the comparison is stated against our digital baseline.
changes.after: Call Sandworms applies to Shai-Hulud drawn after the first in that phase. Placed worms resolve at the end of Nexus. The earlier Dune Zone book handled each Spice pile separately. The original printed faction rule was less clear about restarting the sequence.

changes.before: Use your or your ally's resulting territory
changes.after: Riding a placed worm

changes.before: The new wording permits riding from the territory involved by your or your ally's placed worm. Keep the new shared discard history rather than performing the old independent A/B pile sequence.
changes.after: The new rule allows a ride from the territory affected by your placed worm or your ally's. Use the single discard pile's history, replacing the old separate sequences for piles A and B.

changes.before: Bless the Maker is a drawn-worm effect
changes.after: Bless the Maker

changes.before: The revised one-time power treats the worm as Shai-Hulud drawn during Spice Blow and Nexus. Choose the last normal card's territories or placement through Call Sandworms at the end of Nexus, as the new sheet describes.
changes.after: The revised one-time power counts as Shai-Hulud drawn during Spice Blow and Nexus. As described on the new sheet, use the last normal card's territories or place it through Call Sandworms at the end of Nexus.

changes.before: Nexus was already clarified
changes.after: A Nexus was already allowed

changes.before: The original 2019 Q&A said this Karama worm did not cause a Nexus; the later FAQ corrected it. Our GF9 book already used the corrected Nexus. The new change is its placement and procedure, not merely the existence of that Nexus.
changes.after: The 2019 Q&A said this Karama worm did not cause a Nexus. The later FAQ corrected that, and Dune Zone's book used the correction. The new changes concern placement and the procedure for resolving the worm.

changes.before: If the optional variant is selected, Harj can trigger this same once-per-game power. It does not add a second use or also perform Harj's ordinary move.
changes.after: With Spirit World, discard Harj to use Bless the Maker. This uses the same once-per-game power and does not also give Harj's normal extra move.

changes.before: Battle Edge matches the new combat
changes.after: Free spice strength

changes.before: You automatically receive the spice-strength tier allowed by your dial, without paying spice. You are no longer simply exempt from old force-support costs. Under Classic, the power explicitly returns to full-strength forces without spice.
changes.after: Fremen automatically receives the bonus its force dial qualifies for, without paying spice. This replaces the old exemption from supporting forces. Under Classic, Battle Edge instead lets forces fight at full strength without spice.

changes.before: Fremen contributes 4 force strength plus the automatic +2 spice strength, before its surviving leader. If Karama cancels Battle Edge, it may still pay for spice strength normally.
changes.after: Fremen dials four ordinary forces and gains +2 spice strength for free, before adding a surviving leader. If Karama cancels Battle Edge, Fremen may pay for a bonus normally.

changes.before: Ghola breaks the usual starred-revival cap
changes.after: Ghola may revive several Fedaykin

changes.before: Normal revival still allows only one Fedaykin in the round. Ghola is an explicit exception and can bring back several. Do not extend that exception to every other revival effect.
changes.after: Normal revival still allows only one Fedaykin in the round. Ghola may now revive several. This exception applies to Ghola, rather than to revival effects in general.

changes.before: Special victory now accommodates the ally
changes.after: Special victory allows allied occupation

changes.before: Sietch Tabr and Cave of Birds may be occupied by you, your ally or nobody. An allied Atreides, Harkonnen, Richese or Emperor is exempt from the relevant Tuek's prohibition. The old FAQ specifically refused to count your ally as Fremen for this test.
changes.after: Sietch Tabr and Cave of Birds may be occupied by Fremen, its ally or nobody. Allied Atreides, Harkonnen, Richese or Emperor do not break the relevant Tuek's prohibition. The old FAQ did not count an ally as Fremen for these conditions.

changes.before: The new alliance text explicitly includes allowing worm rides after Nexus. Its revival wording increases the ally's free revival to three total. Our old book already treated that as a total, so do not teach it as a reduction from six.
changes.after: Fremen may allow its ally to ride worms after Nexus. The ally's free revival is three forces in total. Dune Zone's old book already used that total; the change is not a reduction from six.

changes.before: Same special forces
changes.after: Fedaykin remain strength two

changes.before: Fedaykin still has strength two. The new strength comes from the revised free spice tier, not a change to the token's printed value.
changes.after: The Fedaykin token value is unchanged. Fremen gains additional battle strength through its free spice bonus.

changes.before: Emperor: a new alliance bargain
changes.after: Emperor: alliance and revival changes

changes.before: Give spice at phase boundaries
changes.after: Gifts at the end of a phase

changes.before: The old FAQ and our GF9 book allowed immediate gifts at any time. The new sheet allows direct gifts at the end of a phase. That changes whether an ally can use your gift during an auction or midway through its actions.
changes.after: Emperor may now give spice directly only at phase end. The old FAQ and Dune Zone book allowed gifts at any time. An ally must therefore wait until phase end to receive a gift intended for later spending.

changes.before: Keep ordinary contributions separate
changes.after: Auction and shipment contributions

changes.before: Normal permitted allied purchase or shipment contributions still happen at their own payment times. The Emperor's new examples distinguish its contribution sent to the Bank from the ally's own purchase payment received by Emperor.
changes.after: Normal allied contributions still occur when payment is due. In the Emperor's new examples, its contribution goes to the Bank, while the ally's own auction payment goes to Emperor.

changes.before: During bidding
changes.after: Contributing during bidding

changes.before: You may make the ordinary legal contribution to your ally's purchase. That does not create an unrestricted mid-auction gift that the ally can save for a different purpose.
changes.after: Emperor may contribute to an ally's auction purchase under the usual allied payment rules. This is not a direct gift that the ally can keep for another purpose.

changes.before: Extra allied revivals are gone
changes.after: Allied spice strength costs half

changes.before: The old benefit paid for up to three additional allied force revivals. Its replacement halves the ally's cost for spice strength: +2 costs two spice instead of four. This is not a discount on force losses or an extra contribution to the force dial.
changes.after: The old benefit of paying for up to three extra allied force revivals is gone. Emperor instead halves its ally's spice-strength cost. A +2 bonus costs two spice instead of four. Force losses and the force dial are unaffected.

changes.before: War Machine is stronger
changes.after: War Machine revives forces and a leader

changes.before: The one-time power now revives up to four forces, including Sardaukar, and one leader during Revival, outside normal counts. The older power gave up to three forces or one leader. Its extra-Sardaukar permission and Ghola are explicit exceptions to the normal cap.
changes.after: During Revival, the one-time power now revives up to four forces, including Sardaukar, and one leader outside the normal limits. Previously it revived up to three forces or one leader. War Machine and Ghola may revive more than the normal limit of one Sardaukar.

changes.before: Cancellation window
changes.after: Canceling Sardaukar

changes.before: Sardaukar is the vulnerable advantage for the battle. The source table says before plans are made and the sheet says while being formed; both require acting before reveal. It makes them standard forces for that battle, not weaker leaders.
changes.after: Karama makes Sardaukar count as standard forces for that battle. The table says to cancel before plans are made; the sheet says while they are being formed. Both require cancellation before reveal.

changes.before: Atreides: information and the public token
changes.after: Atreides: Prescience and Kwisatz Haderach

changes.before: Spice Vision has a broader written window
changes.after: Spice Vision timing

changes.before: The old sheet inspected at the start of Movement, before anyone moved. The new sheet permits inspection any time during Shipping and Movement. The information effect is familiar, but the printed timing window is broader. The publisher announcement calls the effect unchanged; the intention of that timing difference remains noted for review.
changes.after: The old sheet allowed inspection at the start of Movement, before anyone moved. The new sheet says any time during Shipping and Movement. The publisher describes the ability as unchanged, so it is unclear whether this broader timing is intentional.

changes.before: Prescience asks about the occupied slot
changes.after: Ask which card occupies the slot

changes.before: Ask for the Treachery card in the Weapon or Defense slot, not merely whether a weapon or defense is there. This catches an expansion card occupying that slot even when it is not a weapon or defense. The earlier Ecaz/Moritani rule explicitly concealed Reinforcements and Harass & Withdraw from the narrower question.
changes.after: Prescience asks for the Treachery card in the Weapon or Defense slot, including a card that is not itself a weapon or defense. The earlier Ecaz & Moritani rules concealed Reinforcements and Harass & Withdraw from the narrower question.

changes.before: The force question includes spice strength
changes.after: Ask for force and spice strength together

changes.before: The new named element is the dialed force strength plus spice strength. Do not give the old force dial alone as though it represented the entire force-related contribution. Asking for that element is not permission to inspect the whole plan.
changes.after: The force question now reveals dialed force strength plus spice strength. It no longer reveals just the force dial. Other parts of the plan stay secret.

changes.before: Allied Prescience names both viewers
changes.after: Allied Prescience reveals to both allies

changes.before: The new wording reveals the chosen element to you and your ally. The old sheet named the ally. Legal information sharing already existed, so this is an explicit access clarification rather than an entirely new information trade.
changes.after: The chosen element is revealed to Atreides and its ally. The old sheet named only the ally, although legal information sharing was already allowed.

changes.before: Cancellation window
changes.after: Canceling Battle Prescience

changes.before: Your opponent can cancel Battle Prescience immediately after you name the element, before you receive its answer. It is not an option to wait until you have seen the information and then undo it.
changes.after: Play Karama immediately after Atreides names the element it wants revealed, before receiving the answer.

changes.before: Make the counter public
changes.after: Track battle losses publicly

changes.before: The 2019 sheet said to keep track of losses secretly. In 2.0 you track battle losses publicly, including losses from a traitor call. The threshold remains seven and activation is immediate. This does not add storm or worm deaths.
changes.after: The old sheet told Atreides to track losses secretly. The counter is now public. Kwisatz Haderach still activates immediately after seven battle losses, including traitor losses. Storm and worm losses do not count.

changes.before: Revive the dead token earlier
changes.after: Earlier Kwisatz Haderach revival

changes.before: For two spice, the dead Kwisatz Haderach may use your one leader revival even before normal leader revival has unlocked. Our older GF9 book required normal eligibility. This is a direct change for its readers.
changes.after: For two spice, Atreides may use its one leader revival to revive Kwisatz Haderach before normal leader revival becomes available. The earlier Dune Zone book required normal eligibility.

changes.before: No ordinary leaders have opened revival
changes.after: Kwisatz Haderach dies before leader revival is available

changes.before: The token is dead but normal leader revival is still locked. The explicit 2.0 exception permits reviving the token for two spice. You do not receive an additional ordinary leader revival in the same phase.
changes.after: Atreides may still revive it for two spice. This uses the one leader revival allowed that phase.

changes.before: Golden Path retains its broad target
changes.after: Golden Path is unchanged

changes.before: The once-per-game power still inspects any one player's entire Battle Plan, not just your opponent's. Its immunity to ordinary Karama was already in our older book. The optional new Spirit World trigger is Family Atomics.
changes.after: The once-per-game power still reveals any one player's whole Battle Plan, including a player other than your opponent. Ordinary Karama could not cancel it in the earlier Dune Zone book either. Spirit World adds Family Atomics as an alternative trigger.

changes.before: Retained strengths
changes.after: Other abilities and values

changes.before: Bidding inspection, exclusive written Treachery tracking, the other four battle-leader values and the basic +2 token contribution remain familiar. The new default combat and narrower Karama alter their surrounding decisions.
changes.after: Auction inspection, exclusive Treachery notes, the other four battle-leader values and Kwisatz Haderach's +2 strength are unchanged.

changes.before: One own-traitor redraw
changes.after: Redraw your own traitors once

changes.before: If your initial four include your own leaders, you may reveal and set aside some or all of those, draw that many replacements before other players return their cards, then shuffle the set-aside cards back. Keep the replacements even if they are your own again. It is not a repeated draw until all four are enemies.
changes.after: If the initial four traitors include your own leaders, reveal and set aside any of those you want to replace. Draw replacements before other players return their cards, then shuffle the set-aside cards back. Keep the replacements, even if they are your own leaders again.

changes.before: The new return trigger includes own leaders dead, captured or face-up from earlier battles. The old sheet said all killed. A leader committed elsewhere this round can now help trigger the return of captives.
changes.after: Captives now return when your own leaders are dead, captured or face-up from earlier battles. The old sheet required all your leaders to be killed. Leaders already committed elsewhere this round can therefore count toward returning captives.

changes.before: Cancellation window
changes.after: Canceling Capture Leaders

changes.before: Capture Leaders can be canceled immediately after your battle win, before drawing the captive. Old Karama targets against bonus card draws and allied traitor calls are no longer on the cancellation list.
changes.after: Play Karama immediately after Harkonnen wins, before it draws a captive. Karama no longer cancels bonus card draws or allied traitor calls.

changes.before: Vendetta replaces the old hand theft
changes.after: Vendetta exchanges cards with every player

changes.before: At the end of Bidding, take one random card from every other player and one from the deck. From the combined hand choose one to give to each player, and discard one if you have nine. This replaces the old exchange against one player; it is not the old power applied independently to everyone.
changes.after: At the end of Bidding, take one random card from each other player and one from the deck. Choose one card from the combined hand to give to each player. Discard one if you have nine. This replaces the old exchange with one player.

changes.before: The earlier baseline already had a judgement
changes.after: The old four-card limit

changes.before: The bare 2019 power and later FAQ differed over the maximum taken. Our old book followed the later up-to-four reading. The new table-wide exchange supersedes that disagreement for this power.
changes.after: The 2019 power and later FAQ differed on how many cards could be taken. Dune Zone used the FAQ's up-to-four ruling. The revised exchange replaces that procedure.

changes.before: The source does not fully specify empty hands, an empty deck or every transient hand-limit case in Vendetta. The main exchange is clear; these corner cases remain review questions.
changes.after: The new rule does not fully explain what to do with empty hands, an empty deck or temporary hand-limit problems during Vendetta.

changes.before: Retained setup
changes.after: Unchanged setup and card benefits

changes.before: The eight-card limit, two starting cards, purchase bonus when there is room and four kept traitors remain. Spirit World optionally uses Solaris for the revised one-time power.
changes.after: Harkonnen keeps its eight-card hand limit, two starting cards, bonus draw after a purchase when there is room, and four traitors. With Spirit World, Solaris can trigger Vendetta.

changes.before: Begin with all twenty forces in reserves and eight spice, then make a compulsory Shipping action after setup step five. Bene Gesserit may accompany it. The text does not make it free: use your shipping rules and a legal destination.
changes.after: Start with all twenty forces in reserves and eight spice. After setup step five, make a compulsory paid shipment using the normal Guild rules and a legal destination. Bene Gesserit may accompany it.

changes.before: Five forces to a stronghold
changes.after: Shipping five forces to a stronghold

changes.before: At Guild's reserve-shipment rate, five cost three spice after rounding up. That leaves five spice. You now choose the group and destination rather than receiving five forces fixed in Tuek's. This is a setup action additional to normal round play.
changes.after: Five forces cost three spice at Guild's reserve-shipment rate, rounded up. That leaves five spice. Guild chooses the number and destination instead of receiving five forces in Tuek's. This shipment is in addition to normal round play.

changes.before: The old Guild rate halved normal cross-shipment too. In 2.0 the discount applies to or from off-planet, while cross-shipping is at normal rates. Four forces crossing to a stronghold cost four spice, not two.
changes.after: Guild used to pay half price for cross-shipping. The discount now applies only to shipments to or from off-planet. Four forces cross-shipping to a stronghold cost four spice instead of two.

changes.before: The alliance gains return-to-reserves
changes.after: Allies can return forces to reserves

changes.before: Old FAQ and our GF9 book excluded that option for a Guild ally. The new alliance allows all three shipment types, including a return to reserves and including Fremen. The ally also uses the revised rate distinction: cross-shipping is not half price.
changes.after: A Guild ally may now use all three shipment types, including returning forces to reserves. Fremen may use this benefit too. The old FAQ and Dune Zone book excluded returns to reserves. As with Guild's own shipments, cross-shipping now costs the normal rate.

changes.before: Solaris is a separate question
changes.after: Solaris shipping remains unclear

changes.before: Do not use the broad explanation of Solaris to erase its printed reserve-shipment limit. The main Guild rate changes are confirmed; that card's additional scope is still flagged.
changes.after: Solaris specifies a shipment from reserves on its face, but its explanation refers more broadly to Shipping actions. Whether it also discounts other Guild shipment types is unresolved.

changes.before: Solo Guild compares individual factions
changes.after: Unallied Guild compares individual factions

changes.before: Its new Special Victory Condition requires controlling at least as many strongholds as the single highest faction, even when that faction is allied. It no longer wins merely because everyone else failed to finish.
changes.after: Guild must control at least as many strongholds as the highest individual faction, even if that faction has an ally. It no longer wins simply because no one else won by game end.

changes.before: Allied Guild compares faction or alliance totals
changes.after: Allied Guild compares combined totals

changes.before: With an ally, Guild must match the strongest single faction or alliance total. The allied and unallied comparisons are deliberately different. Refer back to the two examples on the round-ten page.
changes.after: Guild and its ally must together match the strongest faction or alliance. See the examples on the round-ten page.

changes.before: Retain separate checks
changes.after: Special victory and round-ten tie-breaks

changes.before: The Guild special condition is not simply the general fallback tie-break. Normal wins, other special criteria and fallback need their own source checks.
changes.after: The Guild's special condition is separate from the general round-ten tie-breaks. Check normal and special victories before using those tie-breaks.

changes.before: Fold Space remains familiar for Advanced
changes.after: Fold Space is now standard

changes.before: You may still take your whole shipment/movement turn first, last or between players without announcing your plan in advance. This is now part of the unified default for Basic-only veterans.
changes.after: Guild may take its whole Shipping and Movement turn first, last or between other players without announcing the choice in advance. This was an Advanced ability and is now part of the default game.

changes.before: The cancellation deadline matters
changes.after: Cancel before the normal Guild turn passes

changes.before: Karama makes Guild take normal storm order, but cannot be played after its normal turn has passed. Do not wait until Guild has deferred and then attempt to cancel retroactively.
changes.after: Karama makes Guild act in normal storm order. It must be played before Guild's normal turn has passed, even if Guild has chosen to act later.

changes.before: Blockade remains the same one-time job
changes.after: Blockade is unchanged

changes.before: Its special power still stops the specified off-planet shipments. The optional Spirit World trigger is Weather Control. Guild income and its ordinary one-free-revival rate are not newly removed.
changes.after: The one-time power still prevents the specified off-planet shipments. Spirit World adds Weather Control as a trigger. Guild income and its one free revival are unchanged.

changes.before: 2019 p14; second edition pp26,29-33. 2019 p13; second edition pp26,29-30.
changes.after: 2019 pp13-14; second edition pp26,29-33.

changes.before: An optional route to the same power
changes.after: Spirit World

changes.before: Discard the named card instead of Karama to activate your faction's once-per-game power. It is still once per game. Ordinary use or discard of the named card does not trigger the power automatically.
changes.after: With this variant, discard your faction's named card instead of Karama to activate its once-per-game power. Playing or discarding that card normally does not activate the power.

changes.before: It is not another use of the card
changes.after: Use the faction power instead of the card effect

changes.before: Discarding Family Atomics this way does not also destroy Shield Wall. Discarding Harj does not also grant its ordinary extra move. The card supplies the trigger for the faction power, not both effects.
changes.after: Using Family Atomics to activate Golden Path does not destroy Shield Wall. Using Harj to activate Bless the Maker gives no extra move. The discarded card activates only the faction power.

changes.before: It is not another use of the power
changes.after: Still once per game

changes.before: Using Karama earlier does not leave a second Spirit World use available. Nor can you spend a named card for a different faction's benefit or use it as an ordinary cancel.
changes.after: Using the power with Karama also uses up its Spirit World activation, and vice versa. A named card cannot activate another faction's power or be used as a normal Karama cancellation.

changes.before: Default versus variant
changes.after: Choose the variant before play

changes.before: The default game still uses an actual Karama to trigger the one-time power. Decide on Spirit World before play so every player knows which cards are alternate triggers.
changes.after: Without Spirit World, a once-per-game power still requires Karama. Agree on the variant before starting so players know which cards can activate their powers.

changes.before: Choose this instead of default spice strength
changes.after: Classic Spice Dialing

changes.before: Classic Spice Dialing is the retained 2019 Advanced battle system. It replaces the new spice-strength rule. Support a force with one spice for full strength; unsupported forces count at half strength, using the appropriate special-force values and classic loss rules.
changes.after: Classic replaces 2.0 spice strength with the 2019 Advanced support system. Pay one spice per force for full strength; unsupported forces fight at half strength. Use the appropriate special-force values and Classic loss rules.

changes.before: Fremen is explicitly covered
changes.after: Fremen under Classic

changes.before: Under Classic, its Battle Edge returns to full-strength forces without spice. Do not add the new free spice-strength tier on top of that old support exemption.
changes.after: Battle Edge lets Fremen forces fight at full strength without spice. It does not also give the default 2.0 spice bonus.

changes.before: The default 2.0 comparison gives four force strength. Classic gives two unsupported strength. These are alternate rules, not two stages in the same calculation.
changes.after: Four ordinary forces without spice contribute 4 in default 2.0, or 2 under Classic. Use the calculation for the chosen rules.

changes.before: The card pays for spice strength, which Classic replaces. No explicit conversion to old support payment was found. Do not teach unlimited free support as an official ruling.
changes.after: Solaris pays for spice strength. The rulebook does not explain how this works when Classic replaces spice strength with force support.

changes.before: The revised ally benefit discounts spice strength. Its Classic translation is likewise not supplied. The existence of Classic does not automatically rewrite every new faction or expansion exception.
changes.after: Emperor's allied discount also applies to spice strength. The rulebook gives no equivalent discount for Classic support costs.

changes.before: Do not turn a printing error into a rule
changes.after: Errors in the printed examples

changes.before: The source's old wheel illustration includes the retained 8½ display. Some worked examples have inconsistent token wording. New teaching examples should use internally checked arithmetic rather than treating each printed inconsistency as a new mechanic.
changes.after: The rulebook retains an old wheel illustration showing 8½, and some examples use inconsistent token descriptions. These inconsistencies do not describe additional rule changes.

changes.before: Expansion revisions: announced, incomplete
changes.after: Announced expansion changes

changes.before: Keep the base-game comparison separate
changes.after: Old expansions need updated rules

changes.before: Jack Reda explicitly says old expansions were not designed for complete compatibility, naming Karama, Suboid half-dials and Richese sales as mixed-edition decisions. The base book's references to seven other factions look ahead; they do not replace the old sheets.
changes.after: Jack Reda says the old expansions are not completely compatible with 2.0. His examples are Karama, Suboid half-strength dials and Richese sales. Players mixing editions need to agree how those rules work. References to seven other factions in the base book do not replace their older sheets.

changes.before: These announcements do not supply every new number, timing window or exception.
changes.after: Complete rules are still needed for values, timing and exceptions.

before: Choose any starting card from inspected set; suppress to deck top/bottom.
Sequential starting draws with early stop and last-card keep; suppressed card shuffled in.
Face Dancers can revisit factions under the old restrictions.
Battle reveals cannot repeat a target faction. Revival Infiltration deploys up to revealed leader strength.
Six Worthless effects; Karama pays per discarded card.
Some effects strengthen; special Karama adds spice and free revivals.
Occupy contribution and loss calculation before the revised choice.
Optional contribution after reveal avoids losses in thrown battles.
Six Terror tokens; Advanced Assassinate Leaders.
New Ambush removes half an entering group. Execute Leaders has fewer restrictions.
Old cache sale replaces an auction; normally one No-Field.
Larger improved cache, cache card paired with normal auction, extra low No-Field and paired use.
after: Inspect the starting cards and choose any one. Put the excluded auction card on top or bottom of the deck.
Draw starting cards in sequence, with a choice to stop and keep the last card. Shuffle the excluded auction card into the deck.
Battle Face Dancers can target the same faction again under the old restrictions.
Battle reveals cannot repeat a target faction. Infiltration places forces during Revival, up to the revealed leader's strength.
Six Worthless card effects. The special Karama gives spice per discarded card.
Some Worthless effects improve. The special Karama gives more spice and free revivals.
Occupy adds forces to an ally's battle strength, with losses on a win.
Choose whether to contribute after reveal, avoiding losses in deliberately lost battles.
Six Terror tokens and the Advanced Assassinate Leaders ability.
Ambush removes half an entering group. Execute Leaders has fewer restrictions.
